Inflation Runs Hot, Stocks Go Cold
 
Plus, Bank of America posts disappointing results, and investment banks rake in AI-boom cash
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
MICHAEL NAGLE/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

Inflation came in hot. September’s reading of U.S. consumer prices came in higher than economists expected, and remains well above the Fed’s target of 2%. The 3.7% rate came with higher-than-expected core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices. That strengthened the case for the Fed to raise rates once again when its policy-setting body meets in two weeks. The focus for Fed watchers now shifts to Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh’s signaling in an appearance Thursday at IMF meetings in Bangkok.

 

Stocks fell. The inflation report pressured stocks, particularly tech companies at the heart of the AI boom. The Nasdaq fell 1.9%, led by sharp drops in the stocks of AI cloud-computing companies Nebius and CoreWeave. The S&P 500 ended 1.1% lower and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.1%.

 

Bank of America slid. Bank earnings for the third quarter have largely been strong, but Bank of America disappointed. The lender’s profits fell short of analysts’ expectations, even when excluding a $1.2 billion fine imposed over insufficient money-laundering and suspicious transaction controls. Its shares fell 4.8%.

 

Treasury yields spiked. The hot inflation report sent the yield on 10-year Treasury notes above 5.3%, but yields retreated later in the day as stocks declined and investors sought out safer assets.

 
 
 
CONTENT FROM: GOLDMAN SACHS
 
 
How AI is impacting global labor markets
 
Global labor markets are proving resilient even as corporate AI adoption accelerates. While AI-related hiring headwinds are present, they are confined to a narrow set of industries and workers.

One Big Story

 
 
JEENAH MOON/REUTERS
 

Big banks are reaping the rewards of the AI boom in more ways than one. AI-related deals like SpaceX’s IPO are juicing investment-banking fee income. So are fees for debt sales and other transactions tied to the boom. And the millionaires that the AI boom is minting are bringing in another income stream, fueling record revenue in Morgan Stanley’s wealth-management division.

 
 
 

What’s Coming Up

 

• New U.S. retail sales data for September are due Thursday morning.

 

• A September reading of the producer-price index, which measures wholesale inflation, is also due in the morning.

 

• Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is set to speak in Thailand Thursday, but not until 11:30 p.m. Eastern.
